articles.title: An Interstellar Comet's Dust Holds Clues to a Calm, Alien Planetary System
articles.summary: The third known interstellar object, 3I/ATLAS, has a surprise: its dust is almost entirely amorphous, lacking the crystalline silicates found in our solar system's comets. This suggests it formed in a quiet, cold outer region of its home system, revealing that other planetary systems can be strikingly different from our own.

articles.title: Evolution's Surprising Antiviral Strategy: Sea Anemones Use a Brake, Not a Gas Pedal
articles.summary: A newly discovered protein in sea anemones, CARDIB, suppresses the immune system—yet is essential for surviving viral infections. This counterintuitive mechanism reveals that animals evolved multiple, distinct antiviral strategies, challenging the idea of a single inherited defense system.

articles.title: Artificial Light Triggers Massive 'Death Spirals' in Pill Bugs, Study Finds
articles.summary: Streetlights in Israel have been documented luring thousands of land-dwelling isopods into synchronized circular marches, a phenomenon never before observed. The behavior, triggered by the geometry of artificial light, traps the animals in energy-draining loops, leaving them vulnerable to predators and disrupting their natural instincts.
